windows.setup: Run in Windows PowerShell 5.1 at the repository root of a disposable checkout. Create the validation directory, then copy the standalone probe to the listed destination. Use local NTFS storage. Record the revision and filesystem.
expectedResults: The recorded checkout is the worker revision or a verified copy of its source. Windows PowerShell reports 5.1, system tar.exe reports its version, and the workspace volume reports NTFS.

The CLI probe logs alias=true for both case scenarios. The replacement reports one upload and one deletion, installs bytes new at assets, and records only assets in the manifest. The guest-only scenario fails during apply and preserves the sentinel bytes and the previous manifest bytes. Both scenarios remove their auxiliary inputs and lock.

The exact-spelling cases use the ordinary prune list. The native identity test keeps existing distinct directories, skips a missing incoming ancestor and a nested junction with its target, and removes a matching directory chain.

The case-sensitive scenarios report alias=false, remove the tracked leaf, retain Assets/nested and the sentinel when present, and install assets independently. If fsutil cannot enable the flag, record its diagnostic and the skipped case-sensitive scenarios. The distinct existing-directory identity test is an independent control.
Cleanup removes the alias list and continues through all other cleanup inputs when one input is held open.

macos.setup: Run in Bash at the repository root of a disposable APFS checkout. Create the validation directory, then copy the standalone probe to the listed destination. Record the revision and filesystem.
expectedResults: The recorded checkout is the worker revision or a verified copy of its source. The test volume reports APFS and the normalization scenarios log alias=true.

On the normalization-alias volume, the CLI installs the incoming regular file with bytes new, reports one upload and one deletion, and records the decomposed incoming spelling as the only manifest key. With a guest-only file, apply fails and preserves its bytes and the previous manifest bytes. Both runs remove their auxiliary inputs and lock.
The case-only and exact-spelling controls and collision checks pass. The Linux ext4 runs already cover the distinct-normalization control.
